title: CRISPR-based large-scale modeling of loss-of-function mutations to investigate mechanisms of stress resistance in cancer
protocol: Screen human iCas9-expressing clones for editing activity.
Generate knockout populations efficiently and reproducibly across wells.
Transduce doxycycline-inducible Cas9 (iCas9) into the cell line of interest following standard procedures.
Isolate a clonal line to ensure homogeneous editing efficiency.
Identify a clone with high editing efficiency and minimal leaky expression in the absence of doxycycline.
Use a validated sgRNA targeting LMNA for screening isolated clones.
Detect LaminA/C protein through immunofluorescence using a highly-specific antibody.
Quantify knockout efficiency in multiple clones in parallel using high-content microscopy.
Harvest and resuspend hygromycin-resistant, Cas9-expressing MEXF 2090 cells in FACS buffer.
Sort single cells using side and forward scatter into prepared 96-well plates.
Change the media in each plate of clones twice a week.
Begin looking for successful clones after ten days.
Collate clones approaching confluency into three replicate plates.
Dilute pLenti-sgLMNA-GFP lentivirus 1:1 in fresh medium containing 5 μg/mL polybrene.
Add diluted virus to both plates at 100 μL per well.
Incubate the plates for 12–16 hours.
Replace cell culture medium on one plate with medium only and on the other plate with medium containing 1 μg/mL doxycycline.
Incubate for 72 hours.
Prepare fixation solution: 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS.
Prepare permeabilization buffer: 0.5% Triton X in PBS.
Prepare blocking buffer: 3% bovine serum albumin and 0.05% Triton X in PBS.
Fix cells with 100 μL of fixation solution per well for 15 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Discard PFA, wash three times with PBS (5 min each).
Permeabilize with 100 μL of 0.5% Triton X in PBS for 5 minutes.
Remove the permeabilization solution by inverting the plate and add 50 μL blocking buffer per well.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Dilute the primary antibody 1:200 in blocking buffer.
Remove the blocking buffer and add 50 μL of primary antibody dilution per well.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Remove the primary antibody by inverting the plate, and wash three times with PBS.
Dilute the anti-mouse-568 secondary antibody 1:400 in blocking buffer.
Remove the PBS, and add 50 μL per well of diluted secondary antibody.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 30 min, shielding from light.
Remove the secondary antibody, add PBS containing 1.5 μg mL-1 of DAPI and incubate for 5 minutes.
Wash three times with PBS and seal plates.
Image cells using a high-content microscope equipped with standard filter sets for DAPI, FITC, and TRITC.
Identify nuclei using DAPI.
Select GFP + nuclei using the FITC channel.
Measure LaminA/C levels in GFP+ and GFP- nuclei using the TRITC channel.
Set a threshold of LaminA/C signal such that less than 5%-10% of cells in the control, uninfected population are below that value.
Prepare lentiviral plasmid mix for transfection as described.
Leave the plasmid mix at 20°C–25°C for 15 minutes.
Add the transfection mix to each well of HEK293T cells according to library design.
Recover the supernatant containing viral particles after 24 hours post-transfection.
Filter the recovered supernatant through a 96-well filter plate with 0.45 μm pore size.
Repeat recovery and filtration at 48 hours post-transfection for a second batch of virus.
Seal plates containing the viral particles and store them in aliquots at -80°C.
Culture MEXF 2090 cells in complete RPMI medium containing 10% FBS and 1% Pen/Strep.
Trypsinize one 10-cm dish of healthy cells.
Count trypsinized cells.
Seed 5,000 cells per well in a 96-well plate.
Infect seeded cells with viral supernatant diluted 1:8 in RPMI.
Add 5 μg mL−1 polybrene to the viral solution.
Incubate infected plates at 37°C overnight.
Treat MEXF2090 cells with 5 μg mL−1 blasticidin 24 hours post-infection.
Continue selection until control uninfected wells show total death (approximately 4 days).
Split and maintain cell cultures under blasticidin selection as needed.
Discard the medium in 96-well plates by inverting them.
Add 30 μL of trypsin to each well.
Incubate for 4 minutes at 37°C.
Add 80 μL of ice-cold freezing medium (90% FBS + 10% DMSO) to each well.
Seal the plate and store it at −80°C.
Place plates in a water bath at 37°C for a few seconds to thaw cells.
Add 50 μL of medium to each well after thawing.
Spin down the contents at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove 120 μL of liquid from each well.
Add 100 μL of fresh medium to each well.
Replace cell medium with medium containing 1 μg mL−1 doxycycline on day 10.
Culture MEXF 2090 cells in complete RPMI medium containing 10% FBS and 1% Pen/Strep.
Take two 10-cm dishes of healthy cells (70%-80% confluency).
Add 1 μg/mL doxycycline to induce Cas9 expression.
Resuspend the crRNA library in 5 μL/well of 1× siRNA buffer for a 20 μM stock.
Resuspend trRNA in 1 mL for a 20 μM stock.
Add 5 μL of trRNA to each well of the 96-well plate library and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 5 min.
Dilute crRNA/trRNA into 500 μL using OptiMEM to make a 200 nM solution.
Aliquot the diluted solution onto PCR plates (100 μL each) and store at -20°C.
Prepare diluted transfection reagent with 0.3 μL DharmaFECT Duo per 10 μL OptiMEM for MEXF 2090 cells.
Move 10 μL of the diluted crRNA library onto a new 96-well plate.
Add 10 μL of diluted transfection reagent to each well and mix.
Incubate for 15–20 min.
Retrieve Cas9-expressing cells from the incubator.
Trypsinize the cells.
Count the trypsinized cells.
Calculate the volume of cell suspension for 4,000 cells per well in 80 μL complete medium with doxycycline.
Add 80 μL of cell suspension per well in the 96-well plate.
Culture cells for 5 days and expand as necessary.
Add doxycycline to the culture for at least 5 days.
On day 7, the arrayed KO populations are ready to be used for the large-scale fitness assay.
Split confluent arrayed KO plates at a 1:30 ratio to achieve approximately 2000 cells per well.
Grow cells under stressful conditions or maintain them in unperturbed conditions.
Monitor one representative plate throughout the experiment to confirm expected growth kinetics.
Quantify cell numbers by nuclei measurement at the endpoint dictated by stress titration pilot experiments.
Discard medium by aspirating for each plate.
Gently wash cells with PBS.
Add 30 μL of Trypsin and incubate for 5 min.
Add 170 μL of complete RPMI and pipette to resuspend cells.
Transfer the whole suspension of cells to a 2 mL deep well block.
Mix with fresh RPMI medium to achieve the desired dilution.
Transfer 50 μL of cells into new plates containing 50 μL of fresh media.
Gently shake the plate to ensure homogeneous plating.
Discard medium by aspirating.
Gently wash plates with PBS.
Add 100 μL per well of RPMI complete or RPMI with the respective stressor.
Keep outer wells filled with PBS for optimal humidity levels.
Fix plates with 4% PFA at indicated endpoints.
Stain nuclei with SYTOX Green or Red.
Scan whole well in Incucyte® S3 Live-Cell Analysis System.
Remove wells containing cell clumps.
Exclude outliers among replicates that differ from the two consistent replicates by more than three times their difference.
Remove KO populations with severely compromised fitness in unperturbed conditions.
Use the stress/unperturbed ratio in cell count at endpoint to calculate normalized fitness for each KO or control population.
Define KO populations with enhanced or reduced fitness based on the formula Z=(χ-μ)/σ.
Set a z-score > 1.645 for enhanced fitness and < -1.645 for reduced fitness (90% confidence interval).
Perform validation experiments with selected genes exhibiting varying degrees of stress-resistance, including mild phenotypes.
